minutes.headline: Select Board voted that the school's cheaper mini-split AC plan for the primary school is not a substantial change of scope.
minutes.summary: The newly seated board heard public comment, accepted an Eagle Scout food box gift, approved a liquor license manager change, and reviewed a modified air conditioning scope for the primary school. It ratified a planning assistant hire, presented the town manager's composite evaluation, accepted a health insurance opt-out amendment, and reorganized with Jeffries as chair, Alonso vice chair and Nazzaro clerk.

public_comment.topic: Resident from Main Street (Parks Commission requester) urged standards for ARPA funding projects, questioned the vehicle purchases and stormwater project, and argued ARPA should not follow the capital plan process.
Resident (Whiting Street, capital planning committee vice chair) asked whether the primary school electrical infrastructure supports the mini-split plan and raised green communities eligibility.
Finance committee chair questioned power cost, installation quotes, supply chain, absence of an engineer, and contingency if cooling fails.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted that a modified air conditioning scope at the Primary School, using mini-split systems, is not a substantial deviation from the FY23 capital plan.
The board urged the School Committee to get an engineer's confirmation, after hearing that an engineering study is not in the FY24 budget.
The board reorganized, with Jeffries elected chair, Alonso vice chair and Nazzaro clerk, though a new member had asked to postpone.
The board accepted an amendment to the Public Employee Committee agreement creating a health insurance opt-out pilot with incentive payments.
The board ratified a planning department administrative assistant appointment, approved a Lunenburg Liquors manager change and accepted an Eagle Scout food box gift.

why_it_matters: The Primary School cooling plan now proceeds on a cheaper mini-split design within the town meeting appropriation, so residents may be asked later about electrical upgrades, replacement costs or added funding if it falls short.
The health insurance opt-out pilot pays employees not to take town coverage, which affects what the town spends on health insurance and on incentive payments.
watch_next: Water district presents its ARPA request to the Select Board on June 6.
Whether the School Committee obtains an engineer's confirmation of the mini-split plan.

They differ on the chair and vice chair vote results, the AC scope vote, the Lunenburg Liquors vote and the Phase 2 and opt-out figures.
